evidence.finding: Mean logged-in staffing declined 26.7%, from 49 before the incident to 35.9 at/after it; the first drop occurred at 09:15.
Mean productive staffing declined 25.6%, from 45.2 before the incident to 33.6 at/after it.
Scheduled staffing remained fixed at 49, confirming an unplanned realized-staffing gap.
Mean service level fell 23.48 percentage points, from 90.34% to 66.86%.
Mean ASA increased 124.7%, from 25.21 seconds to 56.66 seconds.
Mean abandoned calls rose from 0.6 to 11.1 per interval while answered calls declined.
Incident-period offered volume averaged 2.13% below forecast, excluding a sustained unexpected demand surge.
All queues lost approximately 24.7%–28.9% of staffed agents and all experienced service deterioration, indicating center-wide capacity loss rather than localized misallocation.
A center-wide workforce notice reported multiple same-day absences at 09:15, coinciding with the initial staffing decline.

primary_root_cause_detail: Multiple same-day absences created a center-wide realized staffing shortfall beginning at 09:15. Logged-in staffing subsequently fell from 49 to 33 and productive staffing from 46 to 31, reducing throughput and driving queue growth, higher ASA, abandonment, and sustained service-level degradation.
recommended_actions: Activate same-day absence coverage and cross-skilled reserve staffing when realized staffing falls below requirements.
Set alerts on scheduled-to-logged and required-to-productive staffing gaps, with escalation beginning at incident onset.
Rebalance available cross-skilled agents across queues based on live backlog and ASA until staffing recovers.
Review absence contingency procedures and maintain an on-call or voluntary overtime roster for forecast-critical intervals.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Although offered calls averaged 6.0% above the lower pre-incident actual mean, incident-period demand averaged 2.13% below forecast and showed no sustained surge.
Mean AHT decreased 0.32% after incident start and averaged 0.11% below forecast.
Mean adherence increased from 92.24% before the incident to 93.71% afterward.
Staffing fell proportionally across every queue and all queues degraded, rather than capacity being diverted from one queue.
No platform or routing event was recorded; transfer rates also declined rather than indicating call-processing disruption.

stakeholder_summary: The service-level incident was most likely caused by same-day absences, not excess demand, higher handle time, adherence loss, queue misallocation, or a platform event. The staffing loss began at 09:15 and affected every queue, reducing productive capacity by about 26% and causing sustained wait-time and service-level deterioration.
